focus.jtag: U.S.–Iran hostilities resume in Hormuz, oil spikes, yields at 20-month high
focus.jnote: The environment is hostile on two fronts. Overnight the U.S. and Iran resumed hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz — two oil tankers (one Saudi, one South Korean-owned) were hit by projectiles — and President Trump warned Iran will be hit “at a much harder and higher level” if it retaliates. Oil jumped ~6% to ~$90 WTI (Brent above $90), and the surge in crude fed inflation fear that drove the 10-year yield to ~4.78%, its highest since January 2025. Markets now price a ~66% chance of a September Fed rate hike after Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. Gold slipped ~1% toward $4,375 as yields firmed. This is a live conflict stacked on a hawkish-Fed macro tape — exactly what a Sniper does not sell premium into.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, MPC) and Defense are the groups catching a bid — oil supply fear lifts energy (Marathon Petroleum printed multi-year highs) and conflict-demand lifts defense. But these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers. One de-escalation or Hormuz-reopening headline gaps crude back down and takes energy with it. Watch-only, not table-pounders.
focus.notup: Chips & high-beta tech (Nasdaq −1.03% Mon) and rate-sensitive growth are pressured by the yield spike, and travel/consumer names (Nike, Carnival, Wynn) hit 52-week lows. But selling bear calls into a headline-driven, hike-fear tape carries violent squeeze risk on any peace or dovish surprise — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite sits at 71 (HOT) and P(≥1% gap) at 44% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important: the scanner boarded ZERO names, so there is literally nothing that passed the filters. An active military exchange with an oil shock, plus a 20-month-high 10Y and a live September rate-hike debate, is an unscheduled, open-ended tail you cannot time or size around. Stand down on new credit spreads. Cash is a position today.

risks: Iran retaliation — Trump warned Iran will be hit “at a much harder and higher level” if it responds; any actual strike on U.S. personnel or Gulf bases gaps the whole tape instantly. The number-one thing to watch.
Strait of Hormuz shipping — two tankers were struck by projectiles overnight; a fifth of the world’s oil moves through it. Any closure sends crude vertical — the week’s biggest tail.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI near $90 feeds inflation fear; the 10Y is already at ~4.78%, a 20-month high, and markets price ~66% odds of a September Fed hike. A rate pop compounds pressure on stocks.

ADP (Wed) & Nonfarm Payrolls (Fri 9/4) — a hot jobs print stacked on the oil shock would harden the hike case; a soft print could spark a relief squeeze. Two-sided event risk into a holiday-shortened week.
AVGO (Thu) & the AI/chip complex — Broadcom headlines the tech-heavy slate; single-stock gap risk on top of rate-sensitivity in an already-jittery Nasdaq.

earnings.intro: A tech-heavy slate lands this week: DELL, PANW and MDB reported after Tuesday’s close, with Broadcom (AVGO) Thursday the marquee AI-infrastructure print. With the tape already on edge from the Iran shock and rate-hike fear, a single-stock earnings gap on top of headline risk is a double catalyst — keep every spread clear of its name’s print.
